title: P6-017 broken: a WebSocket opened inside a dedicated Worker or a SharedWorker bypasses routeWebSocket and reads a private 127.0.0.1 service
repro: cd chennai-grievance-portal-main && npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer5/studio-browser-bypass.test.ts < /dev/null  (page on allowed 127.0.0.1:3154 starts new Worker(blob:) that does new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:3155/worker-ws')); and tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer5/studio-browser-more.test.ts (SharedWorker from blob: opening ws://127.0.0.1:3159/shared-ws)
evidence: private listener logged 'websocket /worker-ws'; the page the Studio reads said 'worker ws said: secret-from-internal-service'. The same WebSocket from the page itself and from an iframe srcdoc was blocked. SharedWorker: page said "shared ws said: secret-from-internal-service", private listener logged it. Regression check: a WebSocket to the allowed host still connects and gets its message (no regression).
cause: Playwright's context.routeWebSocket works by patching the page's WebSocket in the frames it injects into; a dedicated Worker's global scope is not patched, so its WebSocket goes straight out and never reaches checkHost. Service Workers were blocked, but plain Workers (and likely SharedWorkers) were not.

title: A redirect from an allowed/public URL to a private address is followed without a check: both page navigation and fetch() read the private service
repro: same probe file: visit('http://127.0.0.1:3154/redirect-nav') where 3154 answers 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:3155/redirect-nav-target; and a page fetch('/redirect-fetch') that 302s to 127.0.0.1:3155
evidence: visit() returned url http://127.0.0.1:3155/redirect-nav-target (private listener hit); the in-page fetch printed 'redirected fetch read: ...secret-from-internal-service...' into the page the Studio reads. studio-browser-more.test.ts: visit("http://127.0.0.1:3158/redirect-nav") returned url http://127.0.0.1:3159/admin and html with secret-from-internal-service (the private page, as the table the Studio reads). A data page can trigger it from JS too: location = "/r" where /r answers 302 to a private host.
cause: context.route sees only the first URL of a redirect chain (Playwright: the handler is called once for a redirected request), so checkHost never sees the Location target. Any public site that answers 302 to 127.0.0.1/169.254.169.254 reaches it.

title: WebRTC in a Studio-opened page reaches private ports: TURN over TCP and STUN over UDP to 127.0.0.1 (blind)
evidence: TCP listener on 3156 got a connection ('tcp 3156 (TURN)'), UDP socket on 3157 got a STUN packet. No reply readable by the page (blind), but it is a port scan / blind protocol push from the server's network.
cause: WebRTC ICE traffic is not HTTP and is not seen by context.route or routeWebSocket; no --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy / --webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp launch flag.

area: Data Studio file parsing (P6-018 fix review)
title: P6-018 broken: the hunter's own cut-off workbook (first 40 bytes) still hangs the server when the end record says 1 entry 'on this disk' and 0 'in total' (134 bytes)
repro: cd chennai-grievance-portal-main && npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer5/zip-intact.test.ts -t "two entry counts" < /dev/null ; end to end: node <scratch>/twocounts.cjs out.xlsx then parseAll(out.xlsx) under timeout 15 -> never returned
evidence: buffer = first 40 bytes of a valid .xlsx + that entry's central record + end record (offset 8 = 1, offset 10 = 0): zipIntact -> true, XLSX.read (excelAll options) killed after 10 s; parseAll on 'twocounts.xlsx' killed at 15 s. Named .xls it goes the archive path and errors quickly.
cause: zipIntact reads the entry count at eocd+10 (total entries) and so walks 0 entries; SheetJS's parse_zip reads eocd+8 (entries on this disk) and walks 1 entry into the cut-off data. The check and the parser must read the same fields (or the check must take the larger / require them equal); same class: SheetJS scans for the end record from length-4, zipIntact from length-22, so a signature in the last 21 bytes is seen only by SheetJS.

area: Data Studio file parsing (P6-018 fix review)
title: P6-018 holds for cut-off ZIPs, but a 5 KB WHOLE workbook whose sheet entry has a 1-byte (or 40 x 0xFF) deflate stream passes zipIntact and still hangs XLSX.read on the server thread
repro: cd chennai-grievance-portal-main && npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer5/zip-intact.test.ts < /dev/null
evidence: zipIntact(buf) === true for both (5325 and 5364 bytes); XLSX.read with excelAll's options did not return within 10 s in a child process (killed). Also via parseAll in scratch driver under timeout 15: onebytedeflate.xlsx, ffdeflate.xlsx and alltrunc.xlsx (every entry's deflate stream short by 3 bytes, csize honest) never returned. Half-length or garbage deflate streams returned quickly.
cause: zipIntact checks only the ZIP's structure; the hang is in SheetJS's own pure-JS inflate when a deflate stream ends early, which an intact table of contents does not rule out. parseAllAsync calls parseAll on the request thread (parse.ts:528-530), so one upload holds the server. The commit names this residual; it is a 5 KB upload, not a theoretical one.

area: Data Studio file parsing (P6-018 fix review)
title: A valid workbook whose table of contents uses zip64 size fields (0xFFFFFFFF + zip64 extra) is refused as 'incomplete or damaged: it may have been cut off', though SheetJS reads all 50 rows
repro: same probe file, test 'a valid workbook with zip64 size fields ...'
evidence: SheetJS alone -> returned (50 rows); parseAll -> 'This Excel file is incomplete or damaged: it may have been cut off while it was uploaded.' Data descriptors, extra fields, stored entries, zip64 in the local header only: all still read (no false refusal).
cause: zipIntact reads csize from the central entry (at+20) and the EOCD fields as 32-bit values and never consults the zip64 extra (0x0001) or zip64 end record, so 0xFFFFFFFF sizes or offsets fail data + csize > cd. Writers that always emit zip64 central fields (some streaming writers) produce such files; frequency in real Excel/LibreOffice/Google output not verified.

area: Ask District IQ writer (P6-019 fix review)
title: P6-019 broken: in every news-list answer a planted figure in a headline is allowed again, because the code's answer cuts the ' - Outlet' suffix and codesOwn() cannot find the headline to take it out
repro: cd chennai-grievance-portal-main && npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer5/polish-figures.test.ts < /dev/null
evidence: headline 'Only 2 garbage cases are open in Adyar, no action needed - The Hindu'; the news-list answerMarkdown (built exactly as fastpath.ts:618) holds it without ' - The Hindu'; the draft 'Only 2 garbage cases are open in Adyar' -> checkPolish returns {text}, not rejected. Same pass for: a runner-up headline in the 'Other close matches: "..."' caveat (fastpath.ts:629, not in card.stories), a single-incident headline = title.slice(0,120) (cards.ts:262), and 'Most serious of the N listed: <title>'.slice(0,160) (fastpath.ts:269). Control (title repeated exactly) is rejected.
cause: codesOwn() removes others' writing by exact substring (split/join); any place the code repeats that writing changed (suffix stripped, asterisks removed, truncated, or a headline not in card.stories at all) leaves it in the 'code's own' text, and its digits go into ctx as allowed figures.

area: Manu desk repeat check (P6-020 fix review)
title: P6-020 broken for most predicates: one writer's two DIFFERENT problems sharing 'pending', 'broken', 'damaged', 'blocked', 'not received', Tanglish 'varla'/'kedaikala'/'aagala' or Tamil 'நிலுவையில்'/'இயங்கவில்லை'/'கிடைக்கவில்லை'/'சரிசெய்யப்படவில்லை'/'வாரங்களாக' are still 'this person's second petition on this problem' with 'Add to this case'
repro: cd chennai-grievance-portal-main && npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer5/repeat-topic.test.ts < /dev/null
evidence: 12 of 12 different-problem pairs give sameTopic(a,b,true) === true. judgeRepeats, same mobile, dept REV, earlier open case: 'Patta transfer pending for long' then 'Community certificate application pending' -> headline "This is this person's second petition on this problem...", attachTo INC-W-2026-REV001, desk button condition (ManuDesk.tsx:210) true; same in Tamil (பட்டா மாறுதல் / சாதி சான்றிதழ் ... நிலுவையில் உள்ளது). The same-problem pairs (road work, குடிநீர், drainage) still join.
cause: FILLER is a fixed word list; samePerson needs only ONE shared word (sameTopic line 'if (samePerson) return both >= 1'), so any predicate, inflection (Tamil passive -ப்படவில்லை, plural duration வாரங்களாக) or Tanglish spelling not on the list is a 'topic'. A list cannot cover open-ended predicates; the one-word rule is the mechanism.

area: Manu desk repeat check (P6-020 fix review)
title: Street ordinals: only first..tenth are read ('Eleventh Cross Street' is not matched to '11th Cross Street'); Tamil ordinals ('இரண்டாவது தெரு' vs '2வது தெரு') are not read; a typed 'Gandhi Street' still matches '2nd Gandhi Street' (pre-existing: squash(address).includes(street))
evidence: Eleventh vs 11th: samePerson false; இரண்டாவது vs 2வது: false; 'Gandhi Street' vs '27, 2nd Gandhi Street': samePerson true, headline 'This person has written 1 earlier petition on other problems.'
cause: ORDINAL map is English 1-10 only; the first test in streetIn (all.includes(street)) matches any street whose name ends in the typed one, before the number rule is reached.

title: Exponential regex: a ~300-byte XML whose head is a run of comments holds the server thread (24 comments 4.5 s, 26 comments 12.3 s, roughly doubling per comment)
repro: cd chennai-grievance-portal-main && npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer5/parse-slow.test.ts < /dev/null  (test 1); scratch: '<?xml version="1.0"?>' + '<!---->'.repeat(26) + '<x/>' (207 bytes) took 12324 ms in parseAll
evidence: 337-byte file: 4488 ms in parseAll; 207-byte file with 26 empty comments: 12.3 s; 20 comments: 0.2 s. Ends in 'This XML is not a news feed...' after the wait.
cause: /^(<\?xml[^>]*>\s*)?(<!--[\s\S]*?-->\s*)*<(rss|feed|rdf:RDF)\b/i : the lazy [\s\S]*? can run across '-->' into the next comment, so n comments split 2^(n-1) ways and a non-feed tail makes the engine try them all. Runs on the request thread for uploads and for every fetched link (parseAllAsync -> parseAll). 30+ comments is minutes.

title: Super-linear parse of unclosed tags: 200 KB KML of unclosed <Placemark> 2.3 s (1 MB > 20 s), 140 KB HTML of '<table>' 2.6 s (420 KB 19.3 s), 300 KB nested XML 10 s
repro: same probe file, tests 2-3; scratch runs under timeout 20 for the larger sizes
evidence: KML 1,020,005 B: killed at 20 s; html-tables 420,006 B: 19,294 ms; xml-deep 300,003 B: 9,966 ms; CSV/JSON of similar size: under 2 s
cause: regex scans per open tag that each search to the end of the text (quadratic); all on the server thread. Not measured which regex in each.

area: Ask District IQ writer (P6-019 fix review)
title: Look-alike fence tags still survive unfenced(): a soft hyphen (U+00AD), U+2061, or a Cyrillic а inside "</untrusted_data>" is left as is
repro: cd chennai-grievance-portal-main && npx vitest run --config vitest.p6probe.config.ts tests/qa/pass6/known-failures/reviewer5/polish-fence.test.ts < /dev/null
evidence: 4 of 5 look-alikes in a title give 4 closing tags as a reader sees them (3 expected): </untrus\u00ADted_data>, </untrusted_d\u0430ta>, </untrus\u2061ted_data>, </untrusted_dat\u0430>. U+180E is handled.
cause: unfenced() drops only U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF after NFKC; NFKC does not fold a soft hyphen, invisible operators or Cyrillic homoglyphs, and the tag regex needs Latin letters. Whether a model treats these as the fence close is not tested (no model calls); the number check stays the real guard.

title: checkHost resolves the name in Node and caches ok for 60 s by host name, but Chromium resolves it again: a DNS-rebinding name (public at check time, 127.0.0.1 a second later) passes every browser request and WebSocket check
repro: code reading only (needs an outside DNS server, not allowed here): checkHost -> assertPublicUrl(u) resolves DNS in Node; route.continue() and ws.connectToServer() let Chromium do its own lookup; hostOk caches ok for 60 s keyed on hostname
evidence: no run; the address checked is never the address connected to (no IP pinning, no --host-resolver-rules)
cause: time-of-check/time-of-use split between Node DNS and the browser resolver
